excerpts.text: **Driskill Mountain** (also referred to as Mount Driskill) is the highest natural summit in [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), with an elevation of 535 ft (163 m) above sea level.[[3]](#cite_note-Heinrich1-3) It lies about 5.3 mi (8.5 km) southeast of [Bryceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryceland,_Louisiana "Bryceland, Louisiana"), in [Bienville Parish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bienville_Parish,_Louisiana "Bienville Parish, Louisiana"). A large [pile of rocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairn "Cairn") marks the high point. When comparing the *highest point* of elevation in each state, this mountain places Louisiana at third lowest - only Florida ([Britton Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britton_Hill "Britton Hill")) and Delaware ([Ebright Azimuth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebright_Azimuth "Ebright Azimuth")) have lower *highest points* of elevation.
